Current funnel is effectively non-existent

Conversion Tracking Gap:

4.6 VAT & Commercial Documents

Saudi VAT (15%) is mandatory on all commercial transactions. If this CRM ever produces quotation documents or invoices, VAT must be built in from day one — not retrofitted.

4.7 Credit Limit & Collection

Outstanding balance

Block on new project creation if customer is overdue

SECTION 7 — UI/UX EVALUATION

Strengths

Clean, professional design system (brand-navy, brand-blue)

Consistent card/input/badge components

Arabic fuzzy search in daily report is excellent

Sidebar navigation is clear and role-aware

Daily report multi-row form is well thought out

Weaknesses

Mobile: The daily report grid (grid-cols-3) on a phone screen will break badly. Saudi sales reps are in the field on their phones. Every data entry form needs to be mobile-first. The 12-field-per-activity row layout is unusable on mobile without a redesign into collapsible cards.

No inline validation: A rep can submit a daily report with no region, no SQM, no contact person. There is no field-level guidance. Basic validation messages would reduce data quality issues significantly.

Pending rep sees full UI: A pending rep who just registered sees the rep sidebar and the daily report form. They can try to submit activities (which will succeed if RLS allows). They should see a "Your account is awaiting approval" screen instead.

No empty states: When a manager opens Customers or Projects (once built), and there is no data, there is no guidance. Empty states with calls-to-action are important for new installs.

No search/filter in any list: Once data grows, every list page needs server-side search, filter by rep/region/status, and pagination.

Team page has no pending badge/counter: The most important UX improvement for the manager is knowing immediately that N accounts are awaiting approval. Currently pending rows are just slightly highlighted in amber.

SECTION 8 — DATABASE & ARCHITECTURE REVIEW

Schema Issues

1. shared_with as text string — architectural flaw
Used in RLS: shared_with ilike '%' || current_rep_name() || '%'. This breaks if:

A rep's name is a substring of another rep's name

A rep is renamed

You need to query "all customers shared with rep X" efficiently

Fix: Replace with a customer_reps junction table:

create table customer_reps (
  customer_id uuid references customers(id),
  rep_id uuid references reps(id),
  relationship text check (relationship in ('primary','shared')),
  primary key (customer_id, rep_id)
);

2. No indexes on foreign keys or query columns
Every join and filter in this app hits unindexed columns:

create index idx_activities_rep_id on activities(rep_id);
create index idx_activities_activity_date on activities(activity_date);
create index idx_activities_rep_date on activities(rep_id, activity_date);
create index idx_customers_primary_rep on customers(primary_rep_id);
create index idx_projects_assigned_rep on projects(assigned_rep_id);
create index idx_projects_stage on projects(stage);
create index idx_reps_auth_user on reps(auth_user_id);

Without these, every dashboard load runs full table scans.

3. activities has no foreign key to projects or customers
Activities are linked via free-text company_name. This breaks any attempt to:

Show all activities for a project

Aggregate SQM accurately per customer

Build customer timeline views

Add: customer_id uuid references customers(id) and project_id uuid references projects(id) to activities (nullable for backward compatibility).

4. rep_monthly_sqm view excludes reps with no activities
The GROUP BY on activity_date means a rep with zero activities this month doesn't appear in the view for the current month. This makes the dashboard SQM bar chart incomplete.

5. month field in activities is stored as formatted text
to_char(activity_date, 'Month YYYY') produces "May      2026" (note trailing spaces from PostgreSQL's month padding). This will cause grouping bugs. Use date_trunc('month', activity_date) for aggregation and format only at display time.

6. Company type mismatch between schema and UI

schema.sql CHECK constraint: Factory, Contractor, Developer, Consultant, Trading, Government, Other

FACET_CRM_CONTEXT.md (after patch): Factory, Advertising, Real State, Owner, Consultant, Contractor, Station Managment, Workshop, Other

app/rep/page.tsx hardcoded TYPES: Factory, Contractor, Developer, Consultant, Trading, Government, Other

Three different lists. The DB patches in context say the constraint was updated but schema.sql on disk still has the old list. This will cause insert failures or silent data quality issues.

Security:

RLS is enabled on all tables ✅

Admin client is correctly isolated to API routes ✅

Anon key is public-facing (correct for Supabase) ✅

Service role key is server-only ✅

No SQL injection risk (parameterized queries via Supabase client) ✅

Risk: current_rep_name() is used in RLS for shared_with matching. If a rep's name contains SQL-like special characters (unlikely but possible), this could behave unexpectedly. Use current_rep_id() for all RLS decisions, never name-string matching.

🟢 Phase 4 — Enterprise & Automation

WhatsApp integration (via n8n + WhatsApp Business API)

Product catalog / price list

VAT-compliant quotation PDF generation

Material submittal tracker

Regional manager role

AI lead scoring and next-action suggestions

Executive revenue dashboard (requires quotation module)

SECTION 10 — MISSING INFORMATION (Questions for the Business Owner)

These are not technical questions — they are business logic questions that directly affect what to build. I need answers before designing several modules:

Sales Process:

When a rep visits a customer who is NOT yet in the system — should they register the customer first (before the daily report), or during the daily report? Currently the flow requires prior registration for autocomplete to work, but free text is still allowed.

Is a "project" always linked to a specific building/site, or can a customer have one project with many quotation rounds? Or many projects per customer per year?

Who creates projects — only the rep, only the manager, or both?

Quotations:
4. Do you currently issue quotations from a separate system (Excel, ERP)? Or should FACET generate the PDF quotation?
5. Do you track quotation revisions? If a quotation is revised 3 times, do you need the history?
6. Are prices per project negotiated individually, or based on a standard price list with discounts?

Shared Customers / Projects:
7. When two reps share a customer, how is SQM credit split? 50/50, or does one rep "own" the project and the other is just CC'd?
8. Can a shared project show up in both reps' personal stats?

Pipeline & Stages:
9. What exactly does "Delivered" mean — product delivered to site, or project fully closed and paid?
10. Is there a credit/collections process? Do you need to track which invoices are paid?

Team Structure:
11. Is there currently only one manager (Zaid Arar), or will there be multiple managers in the future? Will there be a "regional manager" role?
12. Does "Sales Department" (sales@) represent a shared inbox or a real person? How should activities from that account be attributed?

Products:
13. What ACP product lines do you carry? (brand, thickness options, finish types, fire ratings) — needed for quotation module and demand analytics
14. Do you sell non-ACP products (accessories, installation services, fixings)?

Integration:
15. Do you use any ERP or accounting system (SAP, Oracle, Odoo, Zakat authority's Fatoorah)? Any integration requirements?
16. Is the current Google Sheets CRM exportable as CSV for bulk import?

Geography:
17. Do you have physical branches in multiple cities, or is the team all based in one location covering different regions?

Compliance:
18. Do you issue VAT invoices today? Is there an existing invoicing system, or will FACET eventually replace it?

Summary Verdict

FACET CRM has a solid technical foundation: the auth, schema, RLS, and UI system are well-architected for a Phase 1 system. The code quality is clean and consistent. However, as a business operations tool for an ACP supplier in Saudi Arabia, it is currently a daily report submission system with a manager view — not yet a CRM. The gap between what exists and what is needed for real operational use is significant.

The most dangerous current risks are: the company-type data inconsistency, the missing pending-user guard, the shared_with string matching in RLS, and the complete absence of a quotation/value tracking layer — which means management has no financial visibility whatsoever.

The right next move: Fix the 6 immediate issues, then build the core pages in order, and in parallel begin designing the quotation module because every MBA-grade metric you want ultimately depends on it.
